themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints in CD318 spiked to 8 complaints last week versus a baseline of 0.9 per week—an 814% increase (z-score: 4.21)—suggesting a sudden breakdown in sanitation service or a new localized problem that emerged THIS WEEK.
evidence: 8 street sweeping complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (814% spike)
Z-score of 4.21 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Timing aligns with potential service disruption or route change this week
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY (Sanitation) to determine if a route was disrupted, equipment failed, or staffing changed in CD318 this week
Door-knock on affected blocks (residual debris, uncollected refuse) to document visible conditions and get resident testimony

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Spike
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints jumped to 5 complaints 2 weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.5 per week—a 900% spike (z-score: 6.36)—indicating a potential environmental or industrial incident in the district that warrants investigation.
evidence: 5 hazardous materials complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (900% increase)
Z-score of 6.36 indicates very high statistical significance
No follow-up data on whether complaints have subsided or continued; current status unknown
reporting_angles: FOIA the 311 complaint details to identify location(s), nature of materials, and any agency responses (FDNY, EPA, DEP)
Check DEP and NYC Office of Emergency Management incident logs for 2 weeks ago; contact industrial facilities, construction sites, and transportation hubs in the district

themes_detail.label: Illegal Cannabis Retail Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 9 complaints 3 weeks ago versus a baseline of 1.0 per week—an 800% increase (z-score: 9.24)—suggesting a cluster of unlicensed shops opened or became visible to residents in early reporting period.
evidence: 9 cannabis retailer complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly average (800% spike)
Z-score of 9.24 indicates exceptionally high statistical significance
Timing suggests coordinated opening or sudden street-level visibility 3 weeks ago; current count unclear
reporting_angles: Map the 311 complaints to identify which blocks/avenues are hotspots; physical canvassing to locate and document active illegal shops
Interview residents on affected blocks about storefronts, foot traffic, and neighborhood perception; contact SLA and NYPD about enforcement actions and intelligence

themes_detail.label: Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints reached 12 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 2.8 per week—a 336% spike (z-score: 8.49)—indicating a cluster of infrastructure failures or tree-root damage affecting multiple properties.
evidence: 12 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.8 weekly baseline (336% increase)
Z-score of 8.49 indicates very high statistical significance
Clustering suggests geographic concentration; tree maintenance or sewer line issues likely culprit
reporting_angles: Request DEP records on recent sewer breaks, water main work, or tree root damage reports in CD318 from 2 weeks ago
Identify specific blocks with multiple complaints; interview affected homeowners about property damage and repair costs

themes_detail.label: Boiler System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Boiler complaints jumped to 3 complaints 2 weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.5 per week—a 500% spike (z-score: 5.0)—suggesting either seasonal heating issues, equipment failures in multi-unit buildings, or deferred maintenance surfacing.
evidence: 3 boiler complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% increase)
Z-score of 5.0 indicates high statistical significance
Coincides with seasonal drop in temperatures; likely affecting low-income and older multi-family buildings
reporting_angles: Cross-reference boiler complaints with HPD violations and complaint data; identify buildings with repeat failures
Interview affected residents about how long they went without heat; check with tenant advocacy groups for additional complaints
